title: Performance timing
lede: Wall-clock and monotonic timing grouped together, the way real JS/Node group them. The recurring divergence is UTC-everywhere Date: construction, getters, and formatting all ignore local time for deterministic output regardless of machine/CI timezone, and the plain-number Date representation means `-1` stands in for an unparseable date (no NaN) and arithmetic does numeric durations rather than string coercion. performance.now() is a raw CLOCK_MONOTONIC reading with no fixed time origin, and performance.mark/measure are a Map-backed last-write-wins pair with no PerformanceObserver/getEntriesByName machinery behind them.

entries.name: performance.now()
entries.description: A CLOCK_MONOTONIC-based timestamp in milliseconds, as a double (sub-millisecond precision). Unlike Date.now(), it is not tied to wall-clock time, so it is the right choice for measuring elapsed time by subtracting two readings.
differences: No fixed "time origin" like the browser spec (process/page start); returns the raw monotonic reading instead, which is exactly as valid for subtracting two calls to measure elapsed time

entries.name: performance.mark(name) / performance.measure(name, start, end?)
entries.signature: performance.mark(name: string): void; performance.measure(name: string, startMark: string, endMark?: string): number
entries.description: Named timing marks on top of performance.now(), backed by a Map<string, number>. mark(name) records "now" under a name; measure(label, startMark, endMark?) returns the elapsed milliseconds between two marks as a plain number. endMark defaults to the current performance.now() reading when omitted, and measuring against a name that was never marked throws — matching real performance.measure().

returns.desc: Elapsed milliseconds from measure(); mark() returns nothing.

differences: Re-marking a name overwrites its timestamp — last-write-wins, not a full ordered entries list
`measure()` returns the elapsed milliseconds directly as a plain number rather than a `PerformanceMeasure` object, and its own `name` argument is evaluated but not stored anywhere

entries.name: Date
entries.signature: new Date(); new Date(ms); new Date(isoString); new Date(year, month, day?, hours?, minutes?, seconds?, ms?)
entries.description: A thin wrapper over milliseconds-since-epoch. Constructs from no argument (now), a millisecond number, an ISO string, or year/month/day/... fields (month 0-indexed, omitted trailing fields defaulting like real JS). Provides getFullYear/Month/Date/Day/Hours/Minutes/Seconds/Milliseconds, getTime/valueOf, and toISOString.

returns.desc: A Date value (a plain number under the hood).

differences: UTC-only everywhere (construction, getters, formatting) — a deliberate deviation from real JS's local-time default, for deterministic output regardless of the machine/CI timezone; the multi-argument constructor form is a special case of this: real JS treats its fields as *local* time, this compiler always treats them as UTC

entries.name: Date.now()
entries.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, via clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, ...). Wall-clock time, unlike performance.now().
entries.snippet:
const nowMs: number = Date.now()
const now: Date = new Date()

entries.name: Date.parse(string)
entries.description: Parses ISO 8601 strings, with or without milliseconds: Z (UTC), a +HH:MM/-HH:MM timezone offset (converted to UTC), or a bare YYYY-MM-DD date.

returns.desc: Milliseconds since epoch, or -1 if unparseable.

differences: Unparseable input returns `-1` (a documented sentinel — this compiler's Date has no NaN representation)

entries.name: Date setters (setFullYear, setMonth, setDate, setHours, setMinutes, setSeconds, setMilliseconds, setTime)
entries.statusRow: Date setters (setFullYear, setMonth, setDate, setHours, setMinutes, setSeconds, setMilliseconds, setTime)
entries.description: Mutate a named Date variable in place and return the new timestamp, matching real JS.
differences: Requires a named-variable receiver (not a field access or call result — this compiler's Date is a plain number, not a reference object, so there's no heap location to mutate otherwise)
Only the single-argument form of each setter (no `setFullYear(y, m, d)`-style overloads)

entries.name: Date arithmetic (date ± durationMs, date - date, date += durationMs)
entries.statusRow: Date arithmetic (date ± durationMs, date - date, date += durationMs)
entries.signature: date + durationMs; date - durationMs; date - date; date += durationMs
entries.description: Date - Date gives the difference in milliseconds (a number), matching real JS. Adding or subtracting a numeric duration produces a new Date you can keep chaining methods on.

returns.desc: A new Date for ± duration; a number for Date - Date.

entries.snippet:
const start: Date = new Date(0)
const tomorrow: Date = start + oneDayMs
const elapsedMs: number = tomorrow - start
console.log(elapsedMs)                      // 86400000
differences: `Date ± number` gives a new Date (a deliberate deviation from real JS, where `+` on a Date string-concatenates instead — numeric duration arithmetic is far more useful for this compiler's plain-number Date representation)
`Date + Date`, `number - Date`, and compound-assigning a Date into a Date are all rejected at compile time

entries.name: Date.prototype.toDateString()
entries.description: A fixed "Www Mon DD YYYY" shape (e.g. "Thu Jan 01 1970"), matching real JS exactly except for the UTC deviation.

returns.desc: The date as a "Www Mon DD YYYY" string.

entries.snippet:
const launch: Date = new Date(1700000000000)
console.log(launch.toDateString())          // Tue Nov 14 2023

entries.name: Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString()
entries.description: Mimics real JS's default (en-US, no explicit locale) "M/D/YYYY" output.
entries.snippet:
const launch: Date = new Date(1700000000000)
console.log(launch.toLocaleDateString())    // 11/14/2023
differences: One fixed `"M/D/YYYY"` format (the default en-US shape), always UTC; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support
